# Settling paid orders to shops

> When an order is paid, the [`SettlementListener`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/settlement.listener.ts#L23) splits the net amount (total minus platform fee) across the shops in the order and records each shop's share as a credit in the ledger—their balance that they can later claim as a payout.

_Part of [domain/payments](../../units/domain/payments.md)_

Every time an order is marked paid, an `order.paid` event arrives. The settlement listener reads it and extracts all the line items that belong to shops (filtering out platform items). It groups these lines by `shopId` and sums the price of each shop's items to figure out what share of the order came from each shop. The listener then calculates the net settlement amount: the order total minus the platform fee. This net is divided across the shops proportionally to their share using a largest-remainder allocation—a deterministic algorithm that ensures the amounts sum to the exact cent with no rounding loss. The settlement records a double-entry journal: it debits (clears money from) the CLEARING account and credits each shop's account with their share—what we owe them. Because Kafka may redeliver the same event, the listener guarantees exactly-once settlement using three techniques in a single database transaction: a deterministic `journalId` computed as a UUIDv5 of the order ID, a PostgreSQL advisory lock, and an existence check in the ledger. If the settlement has already posted, the check detects it and skips the duplicate. The journal posts through [LedgerService](recording-money-in-ledger.md), which emits a [`JournalPosted`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) event that drives balance reads and payout calculations downstream.

**Look at:** [`SettlementListener` in settlement.listener.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/settlement.listener.ts#L23) · [finance-worker.module.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/finance-worker.module.ts)

## Pieces

- [Largest-remainder allocation algorithm](largest-remainder-allocation.md): The net amount is split across shops by their line total share using an algorithm that distributes remainders to the largest contributors, ensuring sums back to the exact cent with no loss.
- [Exactly-once guarantee with UUIDv5, advisory lock, and existence check](exactly-once-settlement.md): A deterministic `journalId` (UUIDv5 of the order), a PostgreSQL advisory lock, and a transaction-scoped existence check in the ledger prevent duplicate settlements from redelivered Kafka events.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| event | `order.paid` | Triggers settlement. The event payload contains total amount, line items (with `shopId`, price, and quantity), and `paymentId`. |
| database | [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) | Settlement creates entries here: one debiting CLEARING and one crediting each shop's account. The table is also checked for existence to detect redelivered events. |
| event | [`JournalPosted`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) | Emitted by `LedgerService.post()` after the settlement journal records; consumed downstream by balance projections and payout scheduling. |

## Also relies on

- [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md): Calls `LedgerService.post()` to record the double-entry journal that moves money from CLEARING to each shop's account.

## Watch out

- The platform fee ([`PLATFORM_FEE_MINOR`](recording-money-in-ledger.md)) is a fixed amount in minor units (cents), not a percentage—it's subtracted from the total before any allocation happens.
- Shop line grouping and allocation are deterministic only if shops are sorted alphabetically; the code relies on consistent ordering of `shopIds`.
- The advisory lock is transaction-scoped (released at commit or rollback), and the existence check must happen after the lock is acquired in the same transaction—this is what prevents duplicates on Kafka redelivery.
- Lines without a `shopId` are silently filtered out; this includes platform fees, taxes, and any non-shop items.
